outcomes.text: Develop solutions for secure AI system design.
Communicate technical work in writing and speech.
Work effectively as a team member or leader.
Evaluate effects on users and society.

courses.name: Writing and Communications Colloquium
courses.description: Academic writing, textual interpretation, collaborative evaluation and public speaking develop communication and critical inquiry.

category_review.locator: HASS 103 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Written and oral communication are explicit central learning objectives.

courses.name: Research and Entrepreneurship in Computing
courses.description: Faculty and industry seminars examine computing research discoveries and their effects on industries.

category_review.locator: CS 101 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: The seminar spans unspecified computing research fields; the description does not establish a dominant technical subject.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Introductory programming covers design, recursion, object orientation and basic representations and language implementation, with computing ethics.

category_review.locator: CS 115 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Programming and algorithmic thinking organize the introductory computing course.

courses.name: Differential Calculus
courses.description: A seven-week course develops single-variable differentiation and uses derivatives for modeling, optimization and graph analysis.

category_review.locator: MA 121 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation and derivative applications are mathematical methods.

courses.name: Integral Calculus
courses.description: A seven-week course treats integration techniques, improper integrals and integral applications to geometry and mechanics.

category_review.locator: MA 122 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Single-variable integral calculus is the stated subject.

courses.name: First Year Experience
courses.description: New undergraduates develop academic and career habits, leadership, cultural awareness, ethical judgment and wellness while learning university resources.

category_review.locator: PRV 101 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: University transition and personal development combine communication, cultural awareness and career practice without one dominant taxonomy subject.

courses.name: Knowledge, Nature, Culture
courses.description: Students investigate a faculty-selected social or cultural theme from several disciplinary and ethical perspectives and complete a research essay.

category_review.locator: HASS 105 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Social-cultural inquiry and written interpretation establish the human-context focus.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Proof and discrete mathematics are integrated with functional programming.

category_review.locator: Course Description
category_review.rationale: Proof and discrete mathematics are integrated with functional programming.

courses.name: Data Structures
courses.description: Java-based data structures are developed alongside testing, software design representations, searching, sorting and introductory complexity analysis.

category_review.locator: CS 284 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Implementing and analyzing data structures is foundational computer science.

courses.name: Vectors and Matrices
courses.description: A seven-week introduction connects vector geometry, matrix operations, linear equations and eigenvalue methods.

category_review.locator: MA 125 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Vector algebra and elementary linear algebra establish mathematical subject matter.

courses.name: Multivariable Calculus I
courses.description: A seven-week multivariable calculus course covers differentiation, coordinate maps, optimization and double integration.

category_review.locator: MA 126 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Multivariable differential and integral calculus is the central subject.

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Students implement AI problem-solving methods in Python, including search, planning, representation, probabilistic reasoning, learning and language processing.

category_review.locator: CS 367 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly teaches multiple artificial-intelligence methods.

courses.name: Algorithms
courses.description: C++ implementations support analysis of advanced data structures, graph algorithms, sorting and general algorithm design techniques.

category_review.locator: CS 385 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Algorithm design and asymptotic analysis are foundational CS rather than an AI-specific focus.

courses.name: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: Probability theory covers random variables and vectors, distributions, convergence results, Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov models.

category_review.locator: MA 223 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: The course explicitly develops probability theory and stochastic mathematical models.

courses.name: Introduction to Entrepreneurial Thinking
courses.description: Team projects and simulations develop entrepreneurial problem discovery, customer research, business assessment and presentation skills.

category_review.locator: MGT 103 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Substantive entrepreneurship and business-model practice establish an applied business domain; this is not inferred from its place in an AI degree.

courses.name: Data Management and Privacy in AI
courses.description: Data workflows, databases and access control are central.

category_review.locator: Course Description
category_review.rationale: Data workflows, databases and access control are central.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning
courses.description: Mathematical foundations and implemented learning methods share the focus.

category_review.locator: Course Description
category_review.rationale: Mathematical foundations and implemented learning methods share the focus.

courses.name: Statistics
courses.description: Statistical inference includes estimation, testing, regression, experimental design and nonparametric methods, supported by statistical software.

category_review.locator: MA 331 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Statistical methods and inference remain central despite practical software use.

courses.name: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Formal computation models lead to computability limits, reductions and computational complexity.

category_review.locator: CS 334 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Automata, computability and computational complexity are foundational computer-science methods.

courses.name: Human-Centered AI
courses.description: Governance and ethics combine with applied user-experience design.

category_review.locator: Course Description
category_review.rationale: Governance and ethics combine with applied user-experience design.

courses.name: Machine Learning: Fundamentals and Applications
courses.description: Students implement learning algorithms and study supervised and unsupervised methods, neural networks and graphical models.

category_review.locator: CS 559 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: Explicit machine-learning methods establish the AI/ML subject.

courses.name: A.I. and Society
courses.description: Historical, philosophical, social, ecological and political analysis of artificial intelligence.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: AI is the object of social and critical study here; the description does not make this an AI-methods course.

courses.name: Computers and Society
courses.description: Computing in institutions, social relationships and public regulation.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The actual description examines social effects and institutions rather than computational implementation.

courses.name: Ethical Issues in Science and Technology
courses.description: Ethical questions in science and technology, including research conduct, privacy, energy and the environment.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The explicit focus is ethical reasoning about scientific and technological practice.

courses.name: Deep Learning
courses.description: Deep learning methods address visual and language tasks through Python and learning frameworks. The description requires Python and linear algebra; it recommends probability, statistics and numerical analysis but separately lists undergraduate linear algebra and probability as prerequisite preparation.
courses.prerequisites: Python programming and linear algebra are explicitly required. Probability, statistics and numerical analysis are described as recommended, but a later prerequisite statement includes undergraduate linear algebra and probability. See the separately published eligibility rule; neither statement has been silently reconciled. Published eligibility: MA 232 or CS 556 and (Grad Student or (Junior or Senior))

category_review.locator: CS 583 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: The course develops and implements deep-learning methods, not merely a domain application.

courses.name: Senior Design I
courses.description: Teams build software for external clients while learning additional software-engineering techniques as projects require them.

category_review.locator: CS 423 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: General software construction is explicitly described; an AI project is not guaranteed by the host degree.

courses.name: Senior Design II
courses.description: The senior design project continues the CS 423 software-development experience.

category_review.locator: CS 424 Course Information / Course Description
category_review.rationale: The short description explicitly continues CS 423; that separately inspected description establishes team software construction.

courses.name: Mechanics
courses.description: Newtonian mechanics, gravitation, oscillations and waves, using vector methods.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description teaches physical mechanics; quantitative tools support a physics domain course.

courses.name: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Electric and magnetic fields, circuits and electromagnetic theory.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The primary content is physical electromagnetism, not computing infrastructure.

courses.name: Physics Lab I for Scientists
courses.description: Experimental physics with measurement, data analysis and laboratory investigation.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description centers on physical experiments and their measurement; a sequence-wide description is not a claim that this one lab contains every experiment.

courses.name: Biology and Biotechnology
courses.description: Cellular and molecular biology, genetics, evolution and biotechnology.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Substantive biological science establishes the domain category.

courses.name: Biology and Biotechnology Laboratory
courses.description: Practical and simulated experiments supporting introductory biology and biotechnology.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Biological laboratory practice is primary; the source expressly distinguishes this laboratory from medical-school admission requirements.

courses.name: General Chemistry I
courses.description: Introductory chemical principles and quantitative chemical relationships.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The actual description concerns chemical science; the laboratory corequisite does not become another universal AI requirement.

courses.name: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Laboratory experiments supporting introductory chemistry.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Chemical laboratory practice is the primary subject.

courses.name: General Chemistry II
courses.description: Chemical kinetics, equilibria, thermodynamics, electrochemistry and nuclear chemistry.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description establishes substantive chemical science.

courses.name: Quantitative Biology
courses.description: Quantitative biological models using probability, linear algebra and differential equations, with mathematical principles introduced as needed.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly develops both biological understanding and mathematical methods; neither is reduced to a token supporting topic.

courses.name: Introduction to Geosciences
courses.description: Earth systems, geological processes and geoscience applications to natural hazards.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The actual content is earth science and its practical problems.

courses.name: Introduction to Nanotechnology
courses.description: Nanoscale science, fabrication, characterization and devices across physics, chemistry and biology.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Nanotechnology materials and devices establish the domain subject; an AI program association does not make this AI methods.

courses.name: 3D Computer Vision
courses.description: Three-dimensional computer vision, scene geometry, reconstruction and point-set processing.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The described methods address machine perception and three-dimensional visual reconstruction.

courses.name: Health Informatics
courses.description: Health informatics combines healthcare context with information standards, system evaluation, web services and mobile computing.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Healthcare terminology and economics and computing protocols and infrastructure are both substantive in the actual description.

courses.name: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Human-computer interaction principles, interaction models and design methods, with interface design and development projects.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate students: undergraduate data structures and algorithms OR CS 590. Undergraduate students: CS 385.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description combines human interaction and design analysis with software interface construction; preserve mixed content consistently with the reviewed interface courses.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: Visual inference and image-understanding algorithms establish an AI subfield.
courses.prerequisites: Description: undergraduate students require MA232 and CS385; graduate preparation is undergraduate linear algebra and data structures/algorithms, or (MA544 or CS556) and CS590. Student Eligibility Rule: (((MA 544 or CS 556) and CS 590) or (MA 232 and CS 385)) and Graduate Student or At Least Junior

category_review.locator: Course Description
category_review.rationale: Visual inference and image-understanding algorithms establish an AI subfield.

courses.name: Statistical Machine Learning
courses.description: Statistical machine learning for regression, classification, clustering and adaptive learning, including computational and generalization tradeoffs.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: Explicit learning algorithms and their statistical performance establish AI and machine learning content.

courses.name: Causal Inference
courses.description: Causal inference theory and automated methods, including Bayesian networks, time-series causality and logic-based approaches applied to data.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The actual objective is causal inference and its theory; automated implementation and a CS prefix do not by themselves make statistical inference AI.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Natural-language processing with machine-learning and deep-learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate preparation: CS 556 or undergraduate linear algebra and probability.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The actual description explicitly centers on learning methods for language processing.

courses.name: Text Mining and Information Retrieval
courses.description: Text retrieval and mining using ranking models, learned representations and transformer methods.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label
category_review.rationale: The description places modern learned text and language methods alongside information-retrieval techniques.

courses.name: Dynamic Programming and Reinforcement Learning
courses.description: Dynamic programming and stochastic control, including finite- and infinite-horizon models and approximate methods for statistical learning.

category_review.locator: Current public Course Description and title; individual page has no catalog-year label

requirements.summary: Select one published sequence of two science courses and one laboratory; the chemistry/biology row permits a lab alternative.

requirements.title: Math/science electives
requirements.summary: Choose two 3-credit PEP, CH, BIO or MA courses, or the separately named additional options, with prior academic-advisor approval. Required and equivalent coursework is excluded. Published examples of excluded equivalents: MA 117, MA 118, MA 119, MA 134, MA 520. This is an open eligibility rule, not an incomplete finite list.

requirements.title: Technical electives
requirements.summary: Choose the specified number from the published finite pool, with prior academic-advisor approval. A cross-listed label is one option; undergraduate graduate-course access rules also apply.

requirements.title: General electives
requirements.summary: Choose the specified number of Stevens courses carrying at least three credits, with prior academic-advisor approval. Required/equivalent courses and the separately recorded exclusions cannot count. This published open route requires no invented finite course pool.

requirements.title: General-elective exclusions
requirements.summary: Excluded courses: CS 501, CS 515, CS 556, CS 570, CS 573, CS 590 / CPE 590, MA 117, MA 119, MA 134, MA 502.

requirements.title: Pairs that cannot both count
requirements.summary: Do not count both courses in any pair: CS 306 with CS 396; CS 382 with CS 550 / CPE 550; CS 392 with CS 525; CS 488 / CPE 488 with CS 514 / CPE 514; CS 492 / CPE 492 with CS 520; CS 496 with CS 510; CS 442 / CPE 442 with CS 561; SSW 540 with CS 347; CS 346 with CS 546. Cross-listed labels remain one member of a pair.

requirements.title: Humanities policy reference
requirements.summary: Apply the linked university Humanities Requirements, including the AI-specific School of Computing row recorded separately; the program plan and policy describe the same allocations rather than duplicate requirements.

requirements.title: SUCCESS first-year requirement
requirements.summary: Complete the named first-year requirement, subject to the separately published Clark Scholars substitution.

requirements.title: SUCCESS Frontiers choice
requirements.summary: Choose three of the published Frontiers courses.

requirements.title: Undergraduate access to graduate courses
requirements.summary: For 500-level courses, undergraduates need junior standing and course prerequisites; use an A-U section or request an eligibility override with instructor and Graduate Academics approval. For 600+ courses offered by SES or SSB, request permission, attain fifth-semester standing and GPA 3.25, obtain Graduate Academics/advisor approval, and take at most two 600-level courses per semester. The clause scopes the course’s school, not the undergraduate student’s home school; offering units must be checked separately for selected courses.

requirements.title: External-course approval
requirements.summary: While enrolled, request transfer approval before external registration and submit an official transcript; C or better is required. Outside grades do not affect Stevens GPA, even for previously attempted Stevens courses. Full-time Stevens students (12–18 credits) cannot simultaneously take external courses. At most two U.S. humanities courses may transfer while enrolled; upper-level humanities must come from four-year institutions.

requirements.title: University graduation and residency
requirements.summary: Pass required major courses, earn cumulative GPA 2.00 and at least 1.75 across senior-year courses. At least 50 percent of required graduation credits must be completed at Stevens; the transfer policy separately caps transferred credit at 50 percent.

requirements.title: AI humanities distribution
requirements.summary: All undergraduates take HASS 103 and HASS 105. The School of Computing AI row then requires one humanities course, one social science or science-and-technology-studies course, one course from any of those groups, and one of HST 381/HSSC 371/HPL 455. This clarifies the existing plan slots rather than adding duplicate courses. HQSS 300 does not qualify; ECON 243/244 qualify only if not required in the major. The lower language/music/theater/art approval list is explicitly labeled SES/Business, so its applicability to Computing remains unresolved.

requirements.title: Elected pass/fail restrictions
requirements.summary: Pass/fail requires Dean’s List or cumulative GPA 3.50, advisor approval and an extra undergraduate course beyond degree requirements; at most one such course per semester. Graduate courses cannot use pass/fail. Audited courses earn no credit.

requirements.title: Incoming advanced/transfer credit
requirements.summary: Incoming first-year students may receive up to 30 credits from approved AP/IB/A-Level exams or college courses in high school. Transfer students submit prior courses and syllabi for evaluation and construct an academic plan with their advisor; no more than 50 percent of graduation credits may transfer.

requirements.title: Credit by examination
requirements.summary: Full-time undergraduates may seek faculty-approved credit by exam by the fall/spring add-drop deadline. Current students need previous-semester or overall GPA 3.0. A B-or-higher result earns course credit without GPA weight; a failed exam requires regular enrollment. No previously attempted course qualifies. Limits are one exam per semester, eight undergraduate courses and three graduate courses, subject to the published request/approval route.

requirements.title: Course by application
requirements.summary: When a course is not offered, a student may request study by application with instructor and Undergraduate Academics approval after discussing syllabus and assessment arrangements. An approved request receives administrative enrollment and a letter grade; this is an approval route, not permission to replace a required course unilaterally.

requirements.title: Optional overload approval
requirements.summary: No extra courses beyond the first-year academic plan. After year one, Undergraduate Academics may approve one extra class with previous full-time-semester or cumulative GPA 3.30; after an overload semester, GPA 3.6 permits approval for two extra courses. The regular-load threshold is 18 credits. This optional permission does not add graduation credits.

requirements.title: MA 661 offering-school eligibility context
requirements.summary: MA 661 is identified in the current catalog under Engineering and Science. Apply the published undergraduate permission rule for a 600-level SES/SSB course; program listing alone does not waive the GPA, standing or approval conditions.

requirements.title: BIA 665 offering-school eligibility context
requirements.summary: BIA 665 is identified in the current catalog under School of Business (School). Apply the published undergraduate permission rule for a 600-level SES/SSB course; program listing alone does not waive the GPA, standing or approval conditions.

requirements.title: Grade Point Averages
requirements.summary: Cumulative and degree GPAs use the best course attempt; semester GPA includes all graded attempts that term. Each bachelor’s-program course must be passed within three attempts, with W/F counted as unsuccessful; otherwise change to a program not requiring it or withdraw. If a previously passed course is later repeated with F/W, its earlier passing grade remains usable in the graduating GPA. External grades do not enter Stevens GPA.

requirements.title: Academic Standing
requirements.summary: Good standing each semester requires at least 12 earned credits, semester and cumulative GPAs at least 2.000, and at most two withdrawals/failures. The first shortfall leads to Academic Notice and an advised improvement plan; failure to regain good standing during Notice leads to Academic Warning. Notice is available only once; a later shortfall after prior Notice/Warning goes to Warning.
